songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

supporting_acts: Miles Davis Quintet with Airto Moreira

ai_show_review.summary: Epic Dancin' In The Street & fiery Viola Lee Blues fuel a tight groove
ai_show_review.blurb: The show rides a strong groove highlighted by an epic “Dancin' In The Street” and a fiery “Viola Lee Blues.” Jerry’s guitar is snaky and inventive, while Pigpen’s organ adds magical weight to the blues numbers. The rhythm section stays propulsive throughout, making this a must‑listen performance.
ai_show_review.review: On April 12, 1970 at the Fillmore West the Dead delivered one of their most kinetic early‑’70 outings. From the opening “Good Morning Little School Girl” through a seamless “Candyman → Viola Lee Blues,” the band kept a relentless groove, only stumbling on the notoriously sloppy China → Rider transition. The centerpiece is an epic “Dancin' In The Street,” where Jerry’s guitar slithers with peak‑season inventiveness, driven by Phil’s thunderous bass and a propulsive drum jam from Bill (with Mickey locked in tight). Pigpen’s organ shines on “Viola Lee Blues,” adding a magical, weighty texture that lifts the performance to new heights. Highlights also include gritty renditions of “Deep Elem Blues,” the somber “Black Peter,” and the soulful “It’s A Man's World.” The show closes with a chaotic feedback stretch before the gentle encore “And We Bid You Good Night,” cementing this night as a standout moment in the Fillmore era.

rating_calculation.sentiment_rationale: All available analyses are positive, praising Jerry’s snaky guitar on “Dancin'”, Pigpen’s magical organ on “Viola Lee Blues,” the solid rhythm section and a standout drum jam. No consistent negative comments were found; only one song transition noted as sloppy, which does not outweigh the overall enthusiasm.

best_recording.reason: FM broadcast captures the full set with crystal‑clear clarity and excellent instrument separation, making it the most complete and listenable version.

key_highlights: Epic “Dancin' In The Street” showcases Jerry’s inventive lead work.
Fiery “Viola Lee Blues” features magical organ from Pigpen.
Tight rhythm section with a propulsive drum jam that lifts the whole show.
Strong, cohesive groove throughout despite a minor slip on China → Rider.

band_performance.Jerry: His guitar on “Dancin' In The Street” is described as snaky, peak‑season and uniquely inventive.
band_performance.Phil: Provides a driving low end that pushes the jams, especially evident during “Dancin’” and the drum break.
band_performance.Mickey: Locks in with Billy to keep a solid, propulsive pulse throughout the set.
band_performance.Billy: Delivers a tight, propulsive drum jam that’s highlighted as a high point of the show.
